title: Logging In
description: How to sign in to BeautyComm.
content:
Sign in to see your products, orders and reports.

## Purpose

Explain how to sign in to your BeautyComm account.

## Who can use it

Anyone with a BeautyComm account. Your role decides what you see after signing in.

## Where to find it

Open the BeautyComm sign-in page provided to your business.

## Before you begin

* Your sign-in email or username and password.
* A modern, up-to-date web browser.

## Steps

1. Open the BeautyComm sign-in page in your browser.
2. Enter your sign-in details.

<Screenshot step={2} alt="Sign-in page with the sign-in form" label="Sign-in page with the sign-in form" />

3. Select the sign-in button.

## Expected result

You arrive at your dashboard and see the menu items your role allows.

## Notes

* Never share your password.
* If your business uses extra verification, follow the on-screen prompt.

## Common problems

| Problem | What to try |
| --- | --- |
| Wrong password message | Check caps lock, then reset the password if available or ask your administrator. |
| The page keeps reloading | Clear browser cookies for the site and try again. |

## Related guides

* [Logging Out](/docs/getting-started/logging-out)
* [Unable to Log In](/docs/troubleshooting/login-and-access/unable-to-log-in)

3. Use search or filters at the top of a list to narrow what you see.
4. Select a row to open its details.
5. Use your profile or account menu to manage your account or sign out.

## Expected result

title: What Is BeautyComm?
description: A plain-English introduction to BeautyComm, your beauty shop with AI.
content:
BeautyComm is your beauty shop with AI: a commerce platform that helps beauty businesses manage products, stock, orders, customers and sales in one place.

## Purpose

Give you a clear picture of what BeautyComm does before you start using it.

## Who can use it

Business owners, store managers and authorized staff.

## Where to find it

This guide is available in Getting Started in the documentation sidebar.

## Before you begin

* Nothing is required. This is an introduction.

## Steps

1. Read the overview of the platform below.
2. Continue to the platform guide to see how the web application, Admin Panel and mobile app fit together.

## Expected result

You understand the main areas of BeautyComm and where to learn more.

## Notes

* **Catalog and inventory:** keep products, shades and stock up to date.
* **Orders and customers:** follow purchases from placement to delivery.
* **Sales channels and promotions:** sell in more places and run offers.
* **Reports and AI assistance:** understand performance and get suggestions you can review.
* Screens, labels and options can differ depending on your role, plan and BeautyComm version. If something looks different in your account, ask your account administrator.

title: Glossary of Common Terms
description: Plain-English definitions of the terms used across BeautyComm guides.
content:
Short definitions of terms you will meet across BeautyComm guides.

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **SKU** | Stock keeping unit. A unique code that identifies one sellable version of a product. |
| **Variant** | A version of a product, for example a different shade or size. Each variant can have its own SKU and stock. |
| **Attribute** | A property of a product, such as shade, finish or volume. |
| **Catalog** | The full list of products in your shop. |
| **Inventory** | The number of units you have available to sell. |
| **Low stock** | A stock level at or below the point where you should reorder. |
| **Order status** | The stage an order has reached, for example pending, paid or shipped. |
| **Payment status** | Whether an order has been paid, is waiting for payment or was refunded. |
| **Fulfillment** | Preparing and delivering an order to the customer. |
| **Discount** | A price reduction applied to a product or order. |
| **Promotion** | A time-limited offer that may use discounts or codes. |
| **Sales channel** | A place where customers buy from you, such as an online store. |
| **Role** | A set of permissions that decides what a user can see and do. |
| **Integration** | A connection between BeautyComm and another service. |
| **Draft** | An unpublished item, or a documentation page still being verified. |

<Note>Terms in your account may be named slightly differently depending on your BeautyComm version.</Note>

## Related guides

* [What Is BeautyComm?](/docs/getting-started/what-is-beautycomm)

content:
Try these checks when you cannot sign in.

## Purpose

Help you restore access.

## Who can use it

Any user.

## Where to find it

Use this guide from the sign-in page.

## Before you begin

* Your sign-in details.

## Steps

1. Check your email or username for typos.
2. Check caps lock.
3. Reset or retype your password.
4. Clear your browser cookies and try again.
5. Try another browser.
6. Ask your administrator to check that your account is active.

## Expected result

You can sign in.

## Notes

* Contact support if the problem continues. See the guide linked below.

## Common problems

| Problem | What to try |
| --- | --- |
| Account locked | Wait and try again, or ask your administrator. |

* [Logging In](/docs/getting-started/logging-in)
* [How to Contact BeautyComm Support](/docs/support/how-to-contact-beautycomm-support)

title: Adding a Product
content:
Add a product so shoppers can see and buy it.

## Purpose

Walk you through creating a new product with the information shoppers need.

## Who can use it

Users whose role allows creating products.

## Where to find it

Open **Products**, then look for the option to add a product.

## Before you begin

* Product name and description.
* Price and, if you track stock, the starting quantity.
* Product images.
* The category the product belongs in.

## Steps

1. Open the products area and choose to add a new product.

<Screenshot step={1} alt="Add product screen" label="Add product screen" />

2. Enter the product name and description.
3. Set the price and, if used, the SKU.
4. Choose a category.
5. Add images.
6. Add variants such as shades or sizes if the product has them.
7. Save the product. Publish it when you are ready for shoppers to see it.

<Screenshot step={7} alt="Save and publish controls" label="Save and publish controls" />

## Expected result

The product appears in your product list and, once published, in your shop.

## Notes

* Save as a draft if you are not ready to publish.
* Use clear, accurate names so shoppers can find the product.

## Common problems

| Problem | What to try |
| --- | --- |
| Cannot save | Check required fields and look for error messages next to them. |
| Product not visible in shop | Confirm it is published and in stock. |
